name: Lozi
notes: Standard Silozi (Lozi) Latin orthography, standardized by Zambia's Ministry of Education in 1977 alongside Bemba, Nyanja, Tonga, Kaonde, Luvale and Lunda (the seven official Zambian regional languages; Lozi is also the officially promoted regional language of Zambia's Western Province, the former Barotseland). Five-vowel system /a e i o u/. ⟨ch⟩ and ⟨j⟩ spell the single palatal stops /c/ and /ɟ/ (not affricates and not c+h, which would give a stop-plus-glottal-fricative sequence Lozi does not have: AGENTS.md test 1). ⟨sh⟩ is /ʃ/, ⟨ny⟩ the palatal nasal /ɲ/. ⟨ng'⟩ (with a following apostrophe) spells the plain velar nasal /ŋ/, following the same disambiguating convention documented for Zambian Tonga (toi.json) under the shared 1977 harmonized orthography, blocking the wrong maximal-munch read as an ⟨n⟩+⟨g⟩ sequence (AGENTS.md test 3). Smoke-tested against the shared Bantu Zambian-cluster infinitive prefix ku- (e.g. Luvale ⟨kutonga⟩ 'to sew', Tonga íbúsi/ibusu minimal pair) confirming the k-u onset-vowel segments and the s/t/n/m consonant set resolve consistently across the harmonized-orthography sibling languages. Lozi is tonal (high/low, per the harmonized orthography's tone-marking convention) with no lexical word stress; tone is not consistently marked in ordinary orthography and is left unencoded here, a documented exemption distinct from stress (docs/quality_tiers.md).
